successors.name: Danubian Suebi
successors.text: the Suebian kingdom that 'appeared' in northeastern Pannonia after Attila's death in 453 under Hunimund and Alaric; the Marcomanni page does not say the Marcomanni became it

ledger.x: 9 BC: the Marcomanni, under the new king Maroboduus, settle in Bohemia.
20: the displaced Marcomanni come under the Quadian king Vannius.
50: Vannius is deposed and the Marcomanni leave Quadian lordship.
453: the Marcomanni vanish from the page as a polity.

wars.name: Augustus's planned campaign against Maroboduus
wars.outcome: Augustus 'aimed to eliminate the last power center in Germania' in AD 6, but a Pannonian revolt stopped the planned attack; Maroboduus stayed neutral and Tiberius was forced 'to conclude a treaty with Maroboduus and to recognize him as king' (Maroboduus page…

wars.name: War between Arminius and Maroboduus
wars.outcome: War broke out in 17 AD between the two coalitions; after an indecisive battle Maroboduus withdrew into the forests of Bohemia in 18, and was deposed by Catualda in the next year; Tiberius detained him 18 years at Ravenna (died 37).

wars.name: Domitian's Pannonian campaign against the Marcomanni
wars.outcome: Domitian 'was then defeated by the Marcomanni' after a campaign into Pannonia (89 AD).

wars.name: Marcomannic Wars
wars.outcome: Roman victory, 'status quo ante bellum': the Marcomanni and Quadi crossed the Danube (about 169) and were subjugated in 172 and 174; the Quadi rebelled in 177, joined by the Marcomanni; Rome won near Laugaricio (Trencin) in 179; Commodus made peace in 180 and…

wars.name: Diocletian's Marcomannic triumph
wars.outcome: Diocletian 'claimed a triumph over the Marcomanni in 299 AD'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary north of the Danube; the Roman frontier is the Danube.
